text: {"content":"Failed-move cleanup can delete another editor's newer destination revision. Cleanup reads and compares a snapshot, then calls deleteItem. If another edit finishes after that read, storage deletion still removes the item by ID.","codeSuggestion":"","assessment":"P1. Recovery can delete changes made by another editor.","rationale":"removePendingMoveCopies separates getItem and deleteItem at CalTransactionManager.sys.mjs:32–34. Storage deleteItem calls deleteItemById without a revision condition. The storage model also deletes by ID. test_moveRollbackPreservesPendingDestinationEdits changes the destination before cleanup reads it, so it does not cover this interval.","recommendation":"change","validation":"An isolated check executed the exact transaction and storage-provider deletion methods with a controlled storage model. Cleanup received revision 1. The destination then changed to revision 2. Deletion removed revision 2. This proves the method sequence with doubles, not SQLite scheduling.","appliedSummary":"","changeSummary":"Make cleanup deletion conditional on the expected stored revision within the operation that deletes the item. Preserve newer copies. Add coverage for an edit after the cleanup read.","state":"ready","changeAccepted":false,"changeReverted":false,"changesAmended":false}
